name: Fairchild Metroliner / Merlin
variants: SA226 Merlin III / Metro / Metro II
C-26A/B/D/E (Air National Guard and Army counterdrug, ISR and transport)
summary: Slender 19-seat twin turboprop commuter with Garrett engines and a sharp 'shark' nose, also built as the Merlin corporate twin and flown by the US military as the C-26.

wings: Low, straight wing with large span
engines: Two Garrett TPE331 turboprops mounted on the wing in slim nacelles
fuselage: Long, slender, tube fuselage with a sharp pointed nose
Cargo variants have a large rear cargo door; C-26s may carry antennas or a belly sensor
tail: Tall single fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Thin, tube-like commuter fuselage with a very sharp, pointed nose
Low wing with slim turboprop nacelles
Small rectangular cabin windows in a long straight row

confusedWith.howToTell: The 1900 has a T-tail with fins on the tail cone and winglets on the D model, plus PT6 engines in over-wing nacelles; the Metro has a low horizontal tail and a sharper nose.
The Beech 99 has a rounder, blunter nose and a deeper cabin; the Metro has a sharper nose and a more slender fuselage.
The Bandeirante has a more rounded nose and a deeper cabin; the Metro's nose is a sharp point and its fuselage more slender.
